requirements: Each application owns its OS observation and dispatcher; each View owns its framework subscription and handles.

Replacing or throwing from an application callback cannot detach internal View subscriptions. Public configuration callback precedes the public feature/enabled callback; its exception still reaches the caller.
Changes during build/layout/paint/semantics are coalesced to one post-frame update using the latest snapshot. Disposed Views receive no pending update.
Action delivery uses the current View identity. An unrelated View or application receives no action.
OS listener initialization rolls back every successful registration on failure. Stop synchronously gates and removes observers before asynchronous request drain.
An observer returned after a reentrant stop is immediately disposed. Cleanup attempts all registrations and preserves errors.
Native protocol, feature masks, unavailable APIs and query errors are validated; missing producers are not represented as successful empty snapshots.

android.mapping: AccessibilityManager touch exploration -> accessibleNavigation; ANIMATOR_DURATION_SCALE == 0 -> disableAnimations/reduceMotion; AccessibilityManager.isEnabled -> semanticsEnabled

windows.mapping: SPI_GETCLIENTAREAANIMATION -> disableAnimations/reduceMotion; SPI_GETHIGHCONTRAST -> highContrast; SPI_GETSCREENREADER is not used because it does not detect Narrator

differences: Flutter process-singleton/Zone behavior is replaced by app-owned dispatcher and explicit JavaScript callback context.
One pending settings update per View per frame replaces multiple redundant source callbacks. The optional Flutter comparison must remain FAIL for this difference, not be relabeled source parity.
Native OS settings use a bounded shared locale/settings poll per application, plus existing lifecycle/configuration notifications.

FrameworkRoot currently owns a semantics handle throughout its lifetime; platform enabled state owns an additional handle. Optional engine tree toggling is not native acknowledgement. View/native tree submission acknowledgement remains open.
numericPolicy: Feature values and masks must be nonnegative safe integers; unknown bits outside the exact platform mask reject. No Dart numeric wrapper or generated code is introduced.
performance: At most one queued settings notification per View per frame and one 1000ms native poll per observed application. No background polling after stop. Browser integration checks zero retained media-query listeners.
stageBoundary: This contract does not close W9-03 rendering/image/asset recovery, all platform producers or native semantics acknowledgement, nor W9-09 physical reader/IME/FPS acceptance.
